answer: To stop cheap clones multiplying influence, establishment requires a diverse attestation set. An identity only graduates after receiving sealed grades from a terrace of attesters whose prior co-attestation graph is sparse, the way separate chambers in a karst system do not share the same water. If two attesters routinely sign the same cluster, their seals collapse to one vote and both risk a slash of staked collateral. A farm cannot rubber-stamp itself; it has to recruit genuine outside peers, and each missing independent seal leaves its opal deposit locked out of rewards.
